title: F5 warns of six critical BIG-IP flaws in the TMM data plane; hotfixes only
summary: F5 disclosed six critical stack-based buffer overflows in the BIG-IP Traffic Management Microkernel, CVSS 9.8, that can crash the data plane before authentication on specific virtual-server setups, including iRules and one APM policy. The report says they may allow remote code execution. F5 lists no exploitation. Fixes are engineering hotfixes only, with no workaround.
plain: F5 reported six serious flaws in its BIG-IP load balancers that an attacker with no login could use to crash the device, and possibly run code, on certain configurations.
exec: BIG-IP sits at the network edge of many large organisations; hotfix-only fixes mean teams must request builds rather than apply a routine update.
action: Check whether BIG-IP virtual servers use the affected iRules or the APM policy named in F5 bulletin K000164058, request the engineering hotfixes, and restrict exposure of data-plane listeners until patched.

key_findings: Six stack-based buffer overflows in the TMM data plane, CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) and 9.3 (v4.0).
Four reported by watchTowr, two found by F5; no exploitation listed in the advisories.

validation.note: The Hacker News (18 Nov) states the six-flaw count, CVSS, reporters, hotfix-only and no exploitation. Dailysecu (20 Nov) covers only three CVEs and does not state the count, reporters or exploitation, so it does not independently corroborate the core. F5 own portal was not read. GBHackers (21 Nov) covers one of the six, CVE-2026-123637 (APM), and states CVSS 9.8, hotfix-only and no workaround, and makes no claim of active exploitation; it does not state the six-flaw count, so the core stays single-source.

review.note: Compared with The Hacker News and Dailysecu: title, six CVEs, CVSS 9.8, no exploitation, hotfix-only match. Fixed: validation corroborated->single_source (Dailysecu names 3 CVEs, no count/reporters/exploitation); removed occurred_at 10:00Z (no stated time).
